bullets.title: MU: UBS triples PT to $1,625; crosses $1T market cap on +19-22% surge
bullets.body: UBS raised Micron's PT to $1,625, projecting EPS comfortably above $100 through 2029E and ~$400B FCF generation 2027-2029E, citing long-term agreements (LTAs) gaining traction and AI-driven structural memory demand. MU surpassed $1T market cap alongside SK Hynix, with the AI data-center boom driving DRAM revenue near $100B globally in Q1 2026. UBS views LTAs as securing multi-year demand visibility with price floor guarantees.

bullets.title: Semis broad rally: SOXX +5.5%; MU, STX, WDC, MRVL, SNDK hit all-time highs
bullets.body: The semiconductor index posted its strongest day since April 8 on AI demand momentum, with MU +19-22%, MRVL +5.8%, STX +6.3%, WDC +6.3%, AMD crossing $800B market cap for the first time, and SNDK upgraded to OW at Barclays (PT raised to $2,300 from $1,200). JPM is revising datacenter capex estimates up +80% for 2026 and +50% for 2027 with memory accounting for ~30% of hyperscaler capex vs ~8% in 2023-2024. TSMC reportedly eyeing a 15% 3nm price hike in H2 2026 on tight supply.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen commits $150B/yr Taiwan spend; Rubin CPX launch in doubt
bullets.body: CEO Jensen Huang declared NVDA will invest up to $150B annually in Taiwan AI suppliers, calling Taiwan the 'epicenter of the AI revolution.' On the downside, one report flagged NVDA's Rubin CPX inference GPU launch as in doubt with no memory or substrate orders confirmed. NVDA also announced it intends to return ~50% of FCF (~$111B TTM) to shareholders, which Goldman estimates would add 50bps to S&P 500 total cash return.

bullets.title: ZS: -25% post-earnings as FY27 ARR guide 16-17% vs Street 21%; cybersecurity complex under pressure
bullets.body: Zscaler delivered a solid F3Q26 beat (revenue $850.5M, ARR $3.525B, both ahead) but guided FY27 ARR/revenue growth at 16-17% vs consensus of ~19-21%, citing departure of two senior sales leaders and conservative new-logo assumptions. The cybersecurity complex sold off in sympathy: CRWD -4.3%, PANW -4.8%, NET -3.1%, OKTA -3%. Evercore downgraded ZS to In-Line (PT $155 from $225); Piper cut PT to $160; Truist cut to $200; Citi and KeyBanc maintained Buy/OW but lowered estimates. Wolfe kept Outperform, citing 44% valuation discount (5x CY27E revenue) to peers.

bullets.title: SMTC: Beat/raise; data center revenue +85% Y/Y in FQ2; UBS raises PT to $225
bullets.body: Semtech reported FQ1 beat (EPS $0.51 vs $0.48 guide) and guided FQ2 revenue $323-333M, ~10% above Street, on 800G FiberEdge strength and Google Ironwood ACC ramp. Data center now ~50% of revenue, growing 35% Q/Q and 85% Y/Y in FQ2. UBS raised PT from $165 to $225 (32x CY27/28E); Morgan Stanley raised PT to $175. LoRa also accelerating with favorable pricing.

bullets.title: CRM/MRVL/MDB: Key software/semi prints tonight; SNOW least-liked going in
bullets.body: CRM (consensus EPS $3.13, revenue $11.05B) and MRVL (EPS $0.80, revenue $2.41B) report after close today; MDB reports Thursday (EPS $1.19, revenue $664.5M). JPM flags CRM and SNOW as pivotal for software sentiment. DA Davidson expects MDB Atlas growth 28-29% vs 26% guidance with beat/raise potential. SNOW enters as the least-liked of the big three infrastructure names per JPM sentiment tracker; Cortex Code cited as potential revenue accelerant.

bullets.title: APP: META non-IDFA overhang removed; Morgan Stanley sees 50% upside to 2030 revenue
bullets.body: APP surged ~7% after Edgewater noted META is unlikely to pursue non-IDFA iOS bidding before 2027, removing a key competitive threat. Morgan Stanley (OW, $720 PT) argues every 10bp improvement in APP's ~1.3% conversion rate drives ~17% revenue growth; sustaining 20bp annual expansion would yield 34% revenue CAGR through 2030 and put a $1,100 bull case in play. JPM notes APP is now in the 'Consensus Long' quadrant of its tech sentiment matrix.

bullets.title: GOOGL: First 10/10 in JPM tech sentiment; Google commits to fast iteration on AI
bullets.body: GOOGL became the first 10/10 stock in JPM's Tech Sentiment Matrix, described as the most-loved Internet stock and a 'full-stack AI winner.' JPM also notes Google shipping imperfect UX and iterating quickly, with Gemini becoming a control plane as Search/Gemini converge. Separately, GOOGL faces a triple-digit million euro EU fine for DMA antitrust breaches.

bullets.title: INTU: BofA reinstates Buy at $400 PT (31% upside); down ~24% in 5 days pre-note
bullets.body: BofA's Tal Liani reinstated INTU at Buy with a $400 price target implying 31% upside from ~$304; FactSet consensus is $498 average. The stock had declined ~24% over the prior five days. WDAY reinstated at Neutral with $140 PT.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: DOJ set to approve Paramount's $110B WBD takeover; MS double-upgrades PSKY to OW
bullets.body: The DOJ is expected to approve Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery after CEO David Ellison reaffirmed theatrical release commitments; July 15 target close, with a $0.25/share quarterly ticking fee for WBD after September 30. Morgan Stanley double-upgraded PSKY to Overweight and names FWONK as its top 'Live 5' media pick.

bullets.title: SPOT/NFLX/ROKU: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW on all three; SPOT 'King of Media'
bullets.body: JPM names GOOGL, AMZN, SPOT, DASH, and NFLX as top Internet picks. Morgan Stanley reiterates OW on SPOT (AI overhang 'mostly gone'), NFLX, and ROKU. JPM notes NFLX is increasingly a funding short in Media on anemic engagement growth, while RBLX is sharply downgraded with 'almost no bulls left' after a disappointing guide.

bullets.title: EQIX: Morgan Stanley names top pick among Data Center REITs on 'Inference Inflection'
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley positions EQIX as its top pick in data center REITs on an Inference Inflection thesis. Goldman separately highlights CLS (PT $475) as a buy, noting demand exceeds supply across networking and compute with the 800G/1.6T upgrade cycle intact, though supply constraints may limit 2026 upside.

bullets.title: RDDT: DA Davidson Buy with $200 PT; DAU tracking 20.3% vs 18% consensus
bullets.body: DA Davidson reiterates Buy on RDDT with $200 PT, citing DAU growth tracking 20.3% vs 18% consensus and Reddit pixel penetration at 9% vs PINS at 6.3% and SNAP at 5%. The firm sees strong advertising infrastructure competitive positioning.

bullets.title: T: Reaffirms guidance; plans $45B+ shareholder returns 2026-2028; broadband pricing cuts
bullets.body: AT&T reaffirmed long-term guidance and plans to return $45B+ to shareholders via dividends and buybacks through 2028, targeting net debt/EBITDA of ~2.5x post-EchoStar. Q2 FCF guided $4.0-4.5B. JPM's broadband tracker shows AT&T cutting 1/2/5 Gbps pricing by $12/month while raising lower-speed tiers by $5.

bullets.title: TSLA: EU April registrations +46.5% Y/Y; Cybertruck called 'commercial disaster'
bullets.body: Tesla EU+EFTA+UK registrations rose 46.5% Y/Y to 11K units in April, though BYD led at 2.3% market share vs Tesla's 0.9%. Tesla also reported a third consecutive month of strong European monthly sales growth per WSJ. A skeptical X post characterized Cybertruck as a 'commercial disaster' at 10% of targeted production volume.

bullets.title: NOW: CMO departure to OpenAI flagged; Jefferies Software conference presenter
bullets.body: Wolfe notes NOW's CMO is leaving for OpenAI. NOW is presenting at the Jefferies Software, Internet & AI Conference May 27-28 alongside CRM, TEAM, CRWV, WIX, and HUBS. Morgan Stanley also highlights MSFT Azure datacenter capacity expanding from 5GW (FY24) to ~20GW (FY28) to support AI/cloud growth.

bullets.title: CRWD: Oppenheimer raises PT to $750 from $500; new logo and Project Quiltworks in focus
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterated Outperform on CRWD and raised its PT to $750 from $500, citing new logo strength, cross-sell traction, and Project Quiltworks as a long-term monetization vector. Despite ZS-driven sympathy selling (-4.3% premarket), Opco is constructive on CRWD as a beneficiary of any SASE/SSE market share shift.

bullets.title: IREN: $1.6B Dell Blackwell purchase agreement; technical pattern signals potential new uptrend
bullets.body: IREN entered a $1.6B purchase agreement with Dell for Blackwell air-cooled systems, driving the stock +3.9% premarket. Technical commentary on X flags a higher-high/higher-low pattern suggesting a potential new super-cycle uptrend. An X user disclosed a long position entered at $52.

bullets.title: Goldman raises S&P 500 YE target to 8,000; AI infra to drive ~50% of 2026 EPS growth
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its S&P 500 year-end 2026 target to 8,000 from 7,600, forecasting $340 EPS (+24% YoY) in 2026 and $385 (+13%) in 2027. AI infrastructure beneficiaries are expected to account for roughly half of 2026 earnings growth, with valuations anchored near 21x given macro uncertainty. JPM maintains a Tactically Bullish stance and notes June seasonality averages +1.85% (90% hit rate over 10 years).

bullets.title: AVGO: Broadcom reportedly wins xAI/SpaceX ASIC design; MediaTek also cited as contender
bullets.body: Multiple X sources flagged Broadcom as initially favored to design the xAI/SpaceX ASIC, representing a significant revenue opportunity. A separate note cited MediaTek as potentially winning the SpaceX ASIC, with its analyst raising PT to NT$5,520. No official confirmation from either company.
